candidates.title: [3.12] gh-143923: Reject control characters in POP3 commands
candidates.body:
## Before this PR

Python 3.12.16 permits control characters in POP3 commands. If untrusted input reaches a username, password, or another command argument, CR/LF can introduce additional protocol commands (CVE-2025-15367).

## After this PR

==COMMIT_MSG==
==COMMIT_MSG==

This backports [GH-143924](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/143924) to reject C0 control characters and DEL in `_putcmd` before writing to the connection. Ordinary commands retain their existing encoding and wire representation.

### Upstream context

The original change was merged on main, but maintainers [withheld backports because of compatibility concerns](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/143924#issuecomment-3774869691), including passwords containing control characters. A later [3.13/3.14 backport request](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160731) was closed in favor of that discussion.

This PR asks maintainers to reconsider the same policy for 3.12. It does not establish that the earlier compatibility concern has been resolved. The source change follows the existing upstream implementation; the requested decision is whether its rejection behavior is appropriate for this stable branch.

### Validation

The focused `test_poplib` suite completed 74 tests with the changed sources and a Python 3.12 interpreter. Regression coverage exercises all C0 characters and DEL in usernames and passwords for POP3 and POP3_SSL. CPython's configured pre-commit checks passed.

### Review and next steps

1. Seek review from the [`python/email-team` code owners](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.12/.github/CODEOWNERS) in this PR and the existing [GH-143923](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143923) discussion, with an explicit decision on the prior backport objection.
2. If the maintainers and 3.12 release manager accept the compatibility tradeoff, complete the CLA and CI requirements before merge and inclusion in a subsequent 3.12 release.
3. For an idle review, follow the [documented process](https://devguide.python.org/getting-started/pull-request-lifecycle/#reviewing): follow up on the issue after one month, then use Core Development Discourse after a further week without a response.

Refs #143923

## Testing

## Possible downsides?

Credentials containing control characters, such as TAB or backspace, may have worked previously and will now raise `ValueError`. This is the compatibility concern that led upstream to withhold backports.

## Are Docs needed?

* Issue: gh-143923
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

candidates.title: [3.12] gh-143921: Reject unsafe IMAP command characters
candidates.body:
## Before this PR

Python 3.12.16 permits NUL, CR, and LF in IMAP command arguments. If untrusted input reaches an argument, CR/LF can introduce additional protocol commands (CVE-2025-15366).

## After this PR

==COMMIT_MSG==
==COMMIT_MSG==

This backports the corrected argument validation from [GH-153287](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/153287), rejecting NUL, CR, and LF before sending a command. Other control characters remain permitted in explicitly quoted arguments, and message literals retain their existing contents.

The change also adapts the pending literal-state correction from [GH-162017](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/162017). A rejected APPEND must discard its pending message; otherwise a subsequent command can transmit content that the caller was told had been rejected. The literal is captured and cleared before command validation.

### Upstream context

The original [backport decision](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/143922#issuecomment-3774866549) cited compatibility concerns. The narrower validation subsequently landed in 3.13 and 3.14. This PR requests a maintainer decision on applying that narrower guard to 3.12, together with the state-cleanup safeguard; the latter remains under review on main.

### Validation

The focused `test_imaplib` suite completed 110 tests, with 6 skipped, using the changed sources with the released conda-forge Python 3.12.16 interpreter. Coverage includes string and bytes arguments, rejection before sending, legal quoted controls, successful APPEND literals, and command reuse after rejected APPEND calls. The new cleanup regression fails against the previous backport for all six mailbox variants and invalid flags. CPython's configured pre-commit checks passed.

### Review and next steps

1. Obtain protocol and state-management review from the [`python/email-team` code owners](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.12/.github/CODEOWNERS), using [GH-143921](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/143921) and [GH-162010](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/162010) for the existing discussions.
2. Resolve the main-branch follow-up and the 3.12 backport decision with the maintainers and release manager, then complete the CLA and CI requirements before merge.
3. If review remains idle, follow the [documented review process](https://devguide.python.org/getting-started/pull-request-lifecycle/#reviewing): after one month, follow up on the issue; after another week without a response, ask in the Core Development Discourse category.

Refs #143921, #162010

## Testing

## Possible downsides?

Applications that previously supplied NUL, CR, or LF in command arguments will now receive `ValueError`. The pending state-cleanup change requires upstream review alongside the backport.

## Are Docs needed?

* Issue: gh-143921
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

candidates.title: [3.15] gh-154874: Fix the sign of curses.termattrs() (GH-154875)
candidates.body:
## Summary

Backport of GH-154875 to 3.15.

`curses.termattrs()` returns a `chtype` mask, but it was routed through an `int` to check for `ERR`. On a terminal that advertises `A_ITALIC` (topmost bit of a 32-bit mask), the result came back negative and the attribute functions rejected it:

```
>>> curses.termattrs()
-2130771968
>>> curses.newwin(1, 1).attrset(curses.termattrs())
OverflowError: can't convert negative value to unsigned int
```

This returns the mask unsigned via `PyLong_FromUnsignedLong`, matching `getattrs()`, `slk_attr()`, and `term_attrs()`.

The main-branch regression test uses `newterm()` over a pseudo-terminal (`NewtermTestBase`), which is not present on 3.15. The 3.15 test is adapted onto `TestCurses` and skips when the current terminal does not advertise a top-bit attribute.

(cherry picked from commit 0b083c43a455fbdf5378495751e142ea83e294b0)

Fixes #154874

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `test_curses` (requires curses resource)
- Local: full CPython rebuild not run in this environment; change matches main fix in `Modules/_cursesmodule.c` and includes NEWS + adapted unit test.

### AI/LLM disclosure

AI coding tools assisted with the change and this description.

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-154874 -->
* Issue: gh-154874
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->
